_for: 4.0.0_SA_CRO~Z -- key_rulings.json's owner per its own authority line
_why_not_me: infra/logic/** is lane PLATFORM_LOGIC_DOCS, and the issuer has twice ruled this route (the ap-19 row at bb0e3bd764, the nine ap-20 rows at f636989b97). I do not edit the registry.
_append_to: infra/logic/registry/key_rulings.json, the key_rulings array (161 rows at this reading)
_what_the_gate_said: committing infra/aws/terraform/opal-gateway/etfs_read_iam.tf is BLOCKED: '[naming-gate] NAMING REFUSE ... gold/book/* -> {source}/{scope}/gold/book/*  why: NEW and OUT-OF-PATTERN as S3Key: REFUSE', the same for gold/holding/*, platinum/reports/* and silver/holdings/*. NAMING-GATE: REFUSE 7 graded, LGIC_ENFORCE DEC-6, ENFORCE mode. The policy NAME itself graded CONFORMANT as IAM_POLICY.
_what_the_gate_is_grading_and_why_it_mat: these four strings are NOT addresses this code writes or reads: they are FILTER PATTERNS in an IAM s3:prefix condition, whose whole purpose is to CONFINE an s3:ListBucket so it cannot enumerate the bucket. The GetObject ARNs in the same file were not graded, because they are full arn:aws:s3::: strings; only the bare prefix strings look like keys to the limb. Whether a condition's filter pattern is a 'stored-file path' at all is a question for the gate's owner, and it is raised rather than worked around.
_why_these_four_and_not_the_others: MEASURED, not guessed. The limb grades a string only when it has 2+ segments: the single-segment daily/* was not graded at all, and rivalfunds/etfs/gold/* and rivalfunds/etfs/platinum/page/* graded CONFORMANT because rivalfunds/etfs/ happens to satisfy {source}/{scope}/. The four refused are TIER-FIRST (gold/, platinum/, silver/), so they cannot satisfy {source}/{scope}/ by construction -- which is what being legacy means. CONTROL: harvest_read_iam.tf, which I landed 2026-10-14 and which passed this same gate, conditions its ListBucket on bare literals too (packs/, packs/*, wsj/, wsj/*) -- every one single-segment, hence never graded. So the gate's behaviour here is consistent, and this file is the first to put a 2+-segment legacy prefix in a condition.
_not_a_workaround: I did NOT restructure the .tf to build the condition from an HCL expression. The gate defers expressions to plan time, so that would have hidden the literals rather than answered them, and LGIC R30 says a builder refusal is a missing registry row and never a hand-typed workaround. The .tf stays uncommitted until this is decided.

rows._decision_owed: canonical OR none_owed -- 4.0.0_SA_CRO's call, not mine. The contract says a row gives EITHER the whole correct address under key.grammar, OR one plain sentence saying no address is owed from this line and why.
rows._my_reading_offered_not_asserted: none_owed looks right to me, with this sentence: 'The ETFs bucket is tier-first by construction (gold/, silver/, platinum/, daily/) and predates the canon; no address is owed from this line until the ETFs pipeline's own migration project re-addresses the store (02_DOCTRINE.md R19), which is also why the same address carries a legacy_addresses row.' But the registry's owner decides, and a canonical address would be equally actionable for me -- the grant's prefix would then follow it.
